# NIH Censors Crucial Research on Alzheimer's, Kidney Disease, and More, Researchers Share


NIH is targeting and terminating grants for research studies that it thinks will communicate disfavored viewpoints on diversity, gender identity, climate change, and more, violating First Amendment rights and threatening the future of public health.


[Amanda Walgrove](https://www.aclu.org/bios/amanda-walgrove)


**Share This Page**


September 28, 2026


Ann D. Cohen, PhD, was three years into a study on Alzheimer’s disease risk factors when a government agency abruptly terminated her grant. As associate professor at the University of Pittsburgh and co-director of the Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center, Cohen was researching the risk factors of Alzheimer’s disease across racial and socioeconomic groups. But the National Institutes of Health (NIH) targeted her study and pulled her funding because the agency claimed it was “DEI-related research.” As a result, NIH instantly put years of work, millions of dollars, and valuable relationships with community members and colleagues at risk.


“The chaos and scientific loss from this disruption cannot be understated,”[Cohen said](https://www.aclu.org/documents/declaration-of-ann-d-cohen-wilson) , adding that it resulted in “a tremendous loss of data and knowledge.” She said that having to fight the grant termination will be “a tremendous waste of time and intellectual resources during a time where advances in the field are still desperately needed.”


### Stop Censorship and Termination of Scientific Research | American Civil Liberties Union


The Trump administration is unlawfully censoring medical research – cutting off funding for studies on Alzheimer’s, cancer, HIV, and other serious…


[Stop Censorship And Termination Of Scientific Research | American Civil Liberties Union](https://action.aclu.org/send-message/stop-censorship-and-termination-of-scientific-research)


Cohen is just one of many researchers whose work has been censored or terminated by unlawful policies from the NIH, the world’s largest public funder of biomedical research. Under direction from the Trump administration, NIH is systematically trying to silence research-related speech that the administration does not like, on everything from race to gender identity to climate change.


In response, the ACLU, the ACLU of Northern California, Protect Democracy, the Center for Science in the Public Interest, and Jacobson Lawyers Group PLLC have filed[class action litigation](https://www.aclu.org/press-releases/researchers-challenge-nih-screening-of-grants-for-disfavored-viewpoints) challenging the NIH’s ideologically driven censorship, arguing that it violates the First Amendment and federal statutes and regulations. Cohen and other researchers who have had their funding terminated or language censored shared their experiences in court documents.


“The Trump administration is weaponizing control over federal research funding to suppress disfavored ideas, pressuring scientists to censor their work or risk losing funding for research that might produce results that do not conform to the administration’s ideology,” said Rachel Meeropol, senior counsel for the ACLU Racial Justice Program. “This censorship threatens researchers’ fundamental free speech rights and attempts to silence them from pursuing critical research, resulting in the loss of scientific knowledge designed to save lives and advance public health.”


## Terminating Grants Based on Ideology, Not Science


Historically, grant funding decisions have been guided by congressional mandates, regulatory requirements, and scientific expertise — not the ideology of an administration. NIH is changing that.


NIH first attempted to play politics with scientific research in early 2025, issuing a series of directives targeting grants related to “DEI” and “gender identity.” Our ongoing litigation in[APHA v. NIH](https://www.aclu.org/cases/apha-v-nih) successfully challenged those policies and resulted in the reinstatement of hundreds of grants. Despite this, NIH has continued to ideologically censor research. This summer, NIH resumed terminating grants.


NIH is using a troubling list of keywords to identify proposals or grants that it thinks will communicate perspectives this administration does not like. The list of 235 forbidden terms includes “equity” “advancing diversity” “racist” “gender” “Latinx” “climate change” and “pregnant individual,” among others. When the words appear in a grant or application, NIH requires their removal upon threat of grant termination or application denial. Even if researchers comply with the coercion, NIH holds their grant or application for review by political decision makers, not the scientific experts who Congress mandated should make final decisions on grants. This extra-statutory review often leads to extensive delay without updates or the research to be blocked entirely.


[Kelton Minor](https://www.aclu.org/documents/declaration-of-kelton-minor) , for example, received the prestigious NIH Director’s Early Independence Award in 2024 to study the impact of greenhouse gas emissions on human health and behaviors. Upon instruction from the NIH, he rewrote his proposal to remove all mentions of “climate,” “carbon,” and “climate change.” Months later, Minor has still not heard back from NIH and assumes the grant will be terminated at any moment.


“As of today, I have not been able to begin work on the project,” Minor said. “Every additional day of delay that goes by is another day of lost scientific progress and forgone knowledge that could help identify practical opportunities to protect Americans and their health behaviors during periods of extreme temperature.”


[Sara Jackson](https://www.aclu.org/documents/declaration-of-sara-jackson) , a licensed clinical social worker and an assistant professor at the University of Utah, said that she refused to remove what the NIH called “DEI-related language” from her grant award materials upon the agency’s request. She was studying financial hardship among people living with dementia and their care partners, including LGBTQ+ individuals.


“NIH pressure to renegotiate the scope of my award has put me in a very difficult position: to turn my back on my morals, the research I have conducted, the participants who have trusted me with their stories, and the LGBTQ+ community with whom I have worked to build trust,” Jackson said. “Ultimately, I cannot in good conscience erase the stories and identities of my research participants just to ‘align with the new NIH/HHS priorities’ that were not in effect when the grant was awarded.”


Jackon has had no update from NIH since declining to adhere to NIH’s censorship demands and fears her grant will be terminated, forcing her to lay off staff and discontinue her research.


## Preventing Scientific Process and Public Health Advancements


NIH’s reckless actions threaten to undermine decades of scientific progress and disrupt critical research, including research designed to address the needs of underserved populations that disproportionately experience negative health outcomes and some of the most acute health disparities. Its censorship policies will result in the loss of medical knowledge that can help Americans live healthier lives.


[Jonathan Daw](https://www.aclu.org/documents/declaration-of-jonathan-kyle-daw) , professor of Sociology and Demography at the Pennsylvania State University, had his grant terminated while researching why people from different racial and ethnic backgrounds experience kidney disease at different rates.


“Our grant termination is a loss not only for my team and myself,” he said, “but also the broader medical community and for public health, as this type of research is critical to achieving NIH’s mission and making sure we have a healthier society.”


“This unfortunate situation is a loss not only for my team and myself, but also the broader medical community and for public health,” he said, adding that his research “is critical not only to achieving NIH’s mission, but also to making sure we have a healthier society.”


Stymying research into the health disparities faced by LGBT people, racial minorities, and other vulnerable populations from medical research contradicts the fundamental mission of public health and negatively impacts everyone’s health.


“If scientific research does not recruit participants across different demographics, especially including those demographics who have a higher incidence of the disease being studied,” said Cohen about the broad impacts of preventing research, “scientists will not have the information necessary to treat members of all communities effectively.”


## Battling Censorship That Violates the First Amendment


The government cannot manipulate research funding to censor viewpoints based on ideology. Science must be guided by evidence, not a desire to stamp out disfavored views. While NIH can make calls about what topics to fund as long as they’re consistent with statutes and regulations, the First Amendment ensures NIH cannot screen out projects or applicants because it thinks they’ll express views the government does not like.


Our litigation seeks to stop this ideological assault on science in its tracks and reinstate the hundreds of research grants that have not been restored by NIH litigation so far. This lawsuit will seek class-wide relief for all researchers whose work was unjustifiably terminated but have not yet been reinstated by a court order. We won’t stop until this type of censorship ends and grants that’ve been unjustly canceled are restored.

### ACLU Releases Video of ICE Agent Slashing Observers’ Tire


PORTLAND – Two Portland-area residents filed an administrative complaint with the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (“DHS”) today describing how ICE agents tailed and boxed them in with vehicles and slashed their car’s tire after they observed and filmed agents in a parking lot in Hillsboro, a suburb of Portland, Oregon. The video of the agents slashing the tire can be viewed here. The incident took place on October 7, 2026, amid a surge of ICE activity across the state of Oregon. The increase in ICE activity also coincided with a DHS social media post promising to target so-called “sanctuary” jurisdictions like Oregon. It is also the latest example of a pervasive pattern of retaliation against observers occurring all over the country; nationwide, federal agents have intimidated and harassed people observing and filming them in public, including by threatening them, tailing them, pulling them over without reasonable suspicion, surveilling their homes, and even assaulting and arresting them. “What happened to us is not unique, and that is what is so terrifying,” said A.P and M.P., ACLU clients. “We observe and record public ICE activity in order to shine a light on their abusive behavior and to create a record of what our government is up to. Because of that, they are terrorizing us and anyone else who dares to exercise their First Amendment right to hold our government accountable. We hope that sharing our story will bring attention to their reckless and unconstitutional attacks on our communities.” Over the past 18 months, the ACLU and its affiliates have brought several cases, including in Los Angeles, Chicago, and Minneapolis, representing observers who have been surveilled, intimidated, and harassed, for filming federal agents performing their duties in public. Most recently, the ACLU filed a case in Memphis, TN, where a federal task force has been terrorizing local communities for over a year and where observers describe a relentless retaliation campaign against them for filming task force agents. “The right to record publicly visible law enforcement activity is fundamental to our democracy,” said Scarlet Kim, senior staff attorney with the ACLU’s Speech, Privacy, and Technology Project. “Like many people across the country, our clients have been observing and recording ICE activity in their community. These videos have proven critical to exposing ICE’s abuses. If we cannot see and document what our own government is doing on our streets, we cannot hold it accountable for running roughshod over our rights.” “Masked federal officers have no business coming to Oregon to injure or intimidate people,” said Kelly Simon, legal director of the ACLU of Oregon. “Oregonians have the right to support their neighbors and communities by filming and documenting government abuses, and Oregonians should not have to fear retaliation when they exercise their right to record law enforcement.” The complaint demands that DHS investigate the incident, preserve all relevant evidence, and discipline the responsible agents. It further demands that DHS undertake a comprehensive investigation of the nationwide pattern of ICE agents retaliating against individuals observing and recording their activities. You can read the complaint here.

### CAIR and CAIR-Florida Urge Court to Temporarily Block Unconstitutional Terrorism Designation Before More Harm is Done


TALLAHASSEE — The U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida heard arguments today in a lawsuit challenging Florida officials’ baseless and unconstitutional designation of the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) and its Florida chapter as “domestic terrorist organizations.” Unless the court intervenes to prevent it, the largest Muslim civil rights organization in the country will have to shut their doors in Florida on Nov. 5. “CAIR and CAIR-Florida are critical resources that people and institutions across Florida rely on to protect civil rights and liberties, and all we want to do is get back to that important work,” said Hiba Rahim, executive director of CAIR-FL. “Florida’s new law silences free speech, criminalizes association, and eradicates due process, and we are hopeful that the court will act to safeguard our constitutional rights. History reminds us that our country has endured dark chapters, but also that people who refused to accept injustice moved us closer to our founding ideals.” At today’s hearing, the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) urged the court to grant emergency relief for the organizations, explaining the instant and debilitating harm CAIR and CAIR-FL will face if the court does not rescind the designation and stop it from going into effect. In the alternative, they are asking the court to prevent Florida state prosecutors from enforcing the law’s harsh criminal penalties against the nonprofits and third parties who associate with and support them. As the ACLU argued in court, CAIR and CAIR-Florida have done nothing to deserve this devastating designation. The state has never indicted, much less convicted, either CAIR or CAIR-Florida under any criminal law — and certainly not a criminal law involving the serious charge of terrorism. If the state tried to do so, it would fail. The reason is simple: Neither CAIR nor CAIR-Florida is engaged in terrorist activity, and the state would be unable to prove its case to a jury in a court of law. “Florida’s new law is an unprecedented abuse of state authority,” said Ashley Gorski, senior counsel with the ACLU’s National Security Project. “It gives state officials sweeping power to punish American organizations they brand as ‘terrorists,’ without due process and in violation of the First Amendment. We’re asking the court to block this unconstitutional law and ensure that our clients’ crucially important civil rights work serving Floridians is not silenced.” Once a designation becomes effective, an organization’s lawful, constitutionally protected speech and association are immediately rendered illegal and impossible. Under HB 1471, five Florida executive officials have the power to designate and debilitate U.S. groups — including nonprofits engaged in First Amendment-protected advocacy — without filing charges, initiating judicial proceedings, proving their case beyond a reasonable doubt, submitting the case to a jury, or complying with any of the other required constitutional protections of the criminal legal system. An elaborate set of prohibitions makes it a serious crime for the targeted American organization to do virtually anything in the state, and for others to work for or otherwise actively associate with or support the designated group. The consequences of violating these prohibitions are severe, including up to life imprisonment. “Florida’s designation of CAIR and CAIR-Florida flies in the face of fundamental rights guaranteed to all Americans by the Constitution,” said Scott McCoy, deputy legal director at SPLC. “All Floridians should be concerned that this law allows Florida officials to do an end run around the Constitution, shut down disfavored speech and advocacy, and impose draconian criminal penalties. If they are permitted to do it to these civil rights nonprofits, what’s to stop them from doing it to any Floridian with whom they disagree?” The impact on the Floridian communities CAIR and CAIR-Florida serve would also be immense. CAIR-Florida provides a range of pro bono legal services to Florida residents, including those who suﬀer government and workplace discrimination in violation of their civil rights, as well as those navigating the immigration system. “The state does not get to decide whose speech is constitutionally protected or whose due process rights deserve respect. The Constitution decided that long ago,” said Daniel Tilley, legal director of the ACLU of Florida. “And Florida must not strip CAIR and CAIR-FL of their ability to advocate and organize for the civil rights of Floridian Muslims. This dangerous designation regime, crafted by the DeSantis administration, seeks to criminalize protected speech, plain and simple — and with no regard for the harm it causes to the thousands of people our clients support and serve. We are proud to stand with our clients against this abuse of state power.” CAIR and CAIR-Florida are represented by the ACLU, ACLU of Florida, the Southern Poverty Law Center, and Bondurant Mixson & Elmore LLP. This press release can be found here: https://www.aclu.org/press-releases/cair-and-cair-florida-urge-court-to-temporarily-block-unconstitutional-terrorism-designation-before-more-harm-is-done

### Salles, et al. v. National Institutes of Health, et al.


Salles, et al. v. National Institutes of Health, et al. is a class action lawsuit challenging the censorship and termination of federally funded research by the National Institutes of Health (NIH). While ongoing litigation in APHA v. NIH successfully resulted in the reinstatement of hundreds of grants, NIH’s current policies continue to target viewpoints it opposes, threatening research because the government dislikes what it thinks the researchers believe or are likely to say, and continue to violate governing statutes and regulations. This is stymieing critical public health research, particularly related to climate change, the starkest health disparities including those faced by communities of color and LGBTQ+ populations, and other areas.
